messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw 3 nodes in us-west with ECC/Xid spikes this morning. Need a faster way to attribute to card vs. kernel vs. job.

ajay: ugh. are these the same SKUs? can we correlate by GPU serial + kernel oops fingerprint?

maria: yes same 80GB SKU. right now we pull dmesg/journalctl + nvidia-smi dumps, but it's too manual and noisy. thinking a small collector that fingerprints failures.

kevin: what fields would the fingerprint include?

maria: minimal first pass: timestamp window, node, gpu_bus_id, gpu_serial, Xid code, ECC counter delta, PCIe AER errors, last 200 lines of dmesg, last systemd-journal snapshot, process list on GPU, and nvidia-smi -q output.

sara: +1. also capture kernel module version and driver version (nvidia/kepler?). keep a checksum of the dmesg tail so we can group identical stacks.

ajay: agree. for extraction pipeline:
```
# grab kernel dmesg focused on NVRM/Xid and PCIe
journalctl -k -o short-precise --since "-15m" | grep -E "NVRM:.*Xid|GPU ecc|pci .* AER" -n > /tmp/gpu-event.log
# ECC snapshot
nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERFORMANCE,DIAGNOSTIC -f /tmp/nvidia-q-$(date +%s).txt
# small proc map (pid, cmd, cuda_contexts)
nv-smi -x -q  # or query through nvml via python script
```

kevin: maybe avoid full nv-smi XML dumps for all nodes; sample on error only. the agent should have a small ring buffer and ship only on incident.

maria: plan: health-agent watches dmesg/journalctl for keywords (Xid, ECC, oops, gpu-reset), when matched it snapshots the above and posts a short artifact to S3 with metadata + hash. web UI/search can show grouped fingerprints.

rachel: how long do we keep dmesg tails? they get big. also worried about PII in logs (process args).

ajay: store only pid+basename, allow redaction. keep raw logs for 7d, fingerprints and metadata for 90d.

maria: good. another heuristic: compute ECC counter delta since last healthy checkpoint per GPU. sudden jump > threshold => mark as probable hardware. if Xid codes repeat across nodes but same kernel stack -> probable driver/kernel regression.

kevin: we should tag nodes with BIOS/firmware and PCIe link width/speed from lspci -vvv. those seem correlated in past incidents.

ops-bot: automated: node gpu-node-42 drain initiated due to repeated Xid 79 (3 events in 10m) — runbook link: https://runbooks/internal/gpu-drain

maria: thanks ops-bot. i put a WIP RFC in the eng-infra backlog for a lightweight collector + fingerprint service. will prototype one that ships gzipped bundle to s3 and pushes metadata to elastic-search for fast grouping.

rachel: can the prototype also emit a compact JSON fingerprint schema? example fields: {"node","gpu_id","serial","xid","ecc_delta","pci_errors_hash","dmesg_stack_hash","driver_version","timestamp"}

maria: yes. compact JSON + tar.gz artifact. UI will show grouped failures and top-k examples.

ajay: for quick triage checklist (one-pager we can paste into incidents):
- check ECC counters (nvidia-smi -q)
- check Xid code meaning (internal map)
- dmesg tail for NVRM and GPU reset stacks
- check PCIe AER / link problems (dmesg + lspci)
- check kernel/driver versions and recent deploys
- isolate job by draining & repro on spare node

maria: perfect. i'll iterate RFC and ping infra review. hoping this reduces mean time to attribution from hours to <20m.

kevin: if you want i can mock the grouping UI using Kibana maps of fingerprints.

maria: yes please, that'd be great. thanks all. :thumbsup:
